subject: GPU SKU recommendation for Dedicated deployment — sizing & tradeoffs
messages:
From: Aria Gomez <aria.gomez@finex.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: security@finex.com

Subject: Dedicated sizing help — H100 vs A100 vs L4

Hi Karthik,

Quick intro: I run platform at Finex Payments. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a customer-facing chat + embeddings service that will be deployed in a VPC. Before we engage procurement, we need a practical recommendation on GPU SKUs for Dedicated: H100, A100, or L4.

High-level workload notes (attached CSV):
- Mixed workload: 60% short chat completions (~150 tokens), 30% embeddings/indexing, 10% long-context retrieval generation (up to 64k tokens when expanding context).
- Peak concurrency: ~220 concurrent sessions (steady state), occasional spikes to ~600 for short bursts during batch jobs.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms for short chats; long-context can be 1.5–3s.
- Model family: customer leaning toward a 70B opt-style LLM (we may use a quantized variant).
- Compliance: VPC + audit logs required; SOC2 evidence will be requested.

Questions:
1) For a first committed Dedicated cluster, what SKU mix would you recommend (counts of H100/A100/L4)?
2) Tradeoffs we should expect around memory capacity, throughput, and tail latency for the three SKUs?
3) Do you recommend a mixed fleet vs single SKU? Any tips on autoscale/burst configs?

Attach: Finex_inference_workload_v1.csv (sample RPS / token distribution)

Thanks — can we schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through a capacity sketch and an action plan?

Best,
Aria
Aria Gomez
Head of Platform, Finex Payments

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing help — H100 vs A100 vs L4

Thanks Aria — great summary and helpful attachment. Looping in Dev (runtime) and Marissa (solutions) to align on benchmarks and procurement cadence.

Below is a pragmatic recommendation and the reasoning so you can take to procurement. I've kept numbers conservative to give headroom for spikes.

Executive recommendation (initial committed fleet):
- 2 x H100 (for headroom on very large-context/finetuned 70B variants)
- 6 x A100 80GB (workhorse for generation at medium context, better price/perf than H100 in many load patterns)
- 10 x L4 (cost-efficient for short-chat and embeddings; great when you deploy aggressively quantized 4/8-bit models)

Why this mix:
- H100: highest memory bandwidth and large VRAM for 70B models with long KV caches. Use these for the 10% long-context requests and for any heavier fine-tuned checkpoints. They also serve as fallback for high-priority low-latency jobs when A100s are saturated.
- A100 80GB: versatile — you get strong throughput for common generation sequences and enough memory to host medium-length KV caches. Good balance for steady-state traffic.
- L4: much lower cost per GPU for FP16/INT8 inference; ideal for short chats and embeddings. When you quantize models and use Redwood's KV caching and batching, L4s handle the bulk of requests at low unit cost.

Rough capacity/latency expectations (ballpark; we'll validate with a workshop):
- Short chat (~150 tokens): L4 (quantized) ~120–180 requests/sec per card; A100 ~220–300 rps; H100 ~260–350 rps. P95 latency targets: L4 ~80–220ms, A100 ~60–150ms, H100 ~50–120ms for short sequences when not network-limited.
- Long-context (10k+ tokens generation with large KV cache): H100 necessary for reasonable throughput — expect single-digit rps per H100 depending on sequence expansion and attention costs; A100 can handle medium-long contexts but will see higher latency and lower rps; L4s not recommended for very long context without aggressive quantization and sharded runtimes.

Autoscale & burst guidance:
- Provision committed capacity around 70–75% of predicted steady-state to benefit from reserved pricing and keep room for autoscale bursts.
- Configure burst pool to use permissive L4 capacity for short spikes (fast spin-up) and A100/H100 for sustained higher load.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for frequent conversation contexts to reduce repeated compute and shift more volume onto L4s.

Operational asks from Finex for the pilot:
- Provide a short list of 10 representative prompt+context examples for the long-context path and a sample of short-chat traffic shape.
- Confirm regulatory constraints for where GPUs can be hosted (cloud region / on-prem).
- Sign the mutual action plan so we can spin up a small canary cluster.

Attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (sketch of pilot scope, success criteria, initial node counts)

If this looks OK, I'll have Dev run a quick throughput matrix against your sample CSV and we can optimize counts before procurement. I'm available for a call Wed/Thu afternoon.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the thorough breakdown, that format is perfect. A few follow-ups:

- Peak concurrency confirmation: steady ~220, spikes to ~600 for short-chat bursts (these are mostly short requests).
- Long-context distribution: about 12% of requests touch >8k tokens, ~3% exceed 30k.
- Compliance: we need VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS; SOC2 evidence will be requested during procurement.

For procurement, could you translate your recommended initial committed cluster into monthly unit commitments? E.g. the counts you gave (2 H100 / 6 A100 / 10 L4) — what does that look like as committed nodes and a suggested ramp plan over 9 months? Also include an estimate of which SKU will absorb most of our token spend (we want to track unit economics by GPU). If you prefer, your team can draft the ramp and we'll review.

We're available for a call Thu 3pm PT.

Best,
Aria
